getWidget:
/**
 * Typed wrapper around core `getWidget`.
 * Returns `RegisteredWidget` (React-typed) instead of `RegisteredWidgetBase`.
 *
 * @version 0.1.1
 * @since 0.1.1
 */
export declare function getWidget(kind: string): RegisteredWidget | undefined;
validateBlock:
/**
 * Typed wrapper around core `validateBlock`.
 * Narrows `widget` from `RegisteredWidgetBase` to `RegisteredWidget` so
 * canvas components can call `widget.component` without casts.
 *
 * Sound because widgets are only registered via canvas's `registerWidget`,
 * which requires a full `RegisteredWidget` including a React `ComponentType`.
 * `RegisteredWidgetBase.component: unknown` is the schemas layer's React-free
 * escape hatch — the canvas layer re-tightens it here.
 *
 * @version 0.1.1
 * @since 0.1.1
 */
export declare function validateBlock(block: unknown, options?: ValidateBlockOptions): ValidateBlockResult;
CanvasHost:
/**
 * Mount point for agent-rendered canvas widgets.
 *
 * For every block:
 * - Validates envelope + payload against the catalog. Invalid blocks are
 *   dropped with a `console.warn` — the spec mandates "drop, log to admin
 *   audit" on kind/schema failures and never rendering untrusted content.
 * - Renders the registered widget component with a bound `emit` callback.
 *
 * The outer host element is a plain `<div>` — framework-package code is
 * exempt from the apps-convention "no native HTML" rule, and introducing a
 * `Stack` dependency on `@donotdev/components` at the top level would force
 * every consumer to pay for the styled layer even when embedding in their
 * own shell.
 *
 * @example
 * ```tsx
 * <CanvasHost
 *   blocks={turn.canvasBlocks}
 *   onEvent={(e) => agent.emit(e)}
 * />
 * ```
 *
 * @version 0.0.1
 * @since 0.0.1
 */
export declare function CanvasHost({ blocks, onEvent }
